A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MG2-RAG research. All 32 pages of v1 and 34 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, VQA, reasoning, classification, and graph-construction efficiency results, with qualitative examples in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds scalability measurements, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity results, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The textual parsing, entity-driven visual grounding, multimodal node fusion, hierarchical graph, and PageRank retrieval procedures remain unchanged. Section 3 and Appendix A.1 retain the same algorithm and extraction rules; the new ablations evaluate existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate E-VQA, InfoSeek, ScienceQA, and CrisisMMD across the same four tasks. The added analyses vary corpus sizes and configurations within existing coverage; the failure examples remain within the existing VQA scope.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in all corresponding benchmark tables, the efficiency figure, and retained case studies. The new failure cases use the existing VaLiK, MMGraphRAG, and Qwen3.5-27B comparators; added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with component-removal controls, E-VQA (5k) retrieval-parameter sweeps, and construction-time measurements from 1k to 100k documents with a doubled-GPU condition (Tables 1, 6, and 8–11). These are additional protocols; the original splits, metrics, backbone configurations, prompts, and default hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: v1 has successful case studies but no component ablations or parameter sensitivity tests. v2 adds ablations of hierarchy, node fusion, and propagation across multiple tasks, four sensitivity analyses, construction scalability tests, and two failure cases examining ambiguous visual references.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new analyses continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 1–4 exactly match v2 Tables 2–5 in reported scores. Substantial new results include E-VQA (5k) R@1 of 57.8 versus 25.5 without propagation, sensitivity measurements, failure outcomes, and 100k construction times of 63.4 hours versus 32.8 with doubled GPUs. These are added results, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, incidence matrices, aggregation and fusion equations, PageRank update, and appendix relation-extraction formulations are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same lightweight construction, modality-preserving fusion, and graph-retrieval contributions. The four-task state-of-the-art claim and average 43.3× speedup and 23.9× cost reduction are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of component complementarity, parameter robustness, scalability, and coarse-context support when grounding is imperfect. Appendix B also introduces an explicit failure mechanism: ambiguous visual references weaken entity grounding and propagation, allowing plausible but factually incorrect evidence to dominate. This substantially expands the earlier success-focused discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public source-code availability statement and repository address in the abstract, plus parameter ranges and hardware conditions for the new analyses. Existing implementation descriptions, preprocessing instructions, prompts, and default hyperparameters remain unchanged; repository availability itself is not verified by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Eight cited works are added, including Simple is Effective, Think-on-Graph 2.0, and Subgraph Retrieval Enhanced Model. Section 2 expands discussion of lightweight triple scoring and decoupled subgraph retrieval while retaining the same overall positioning. Publication and bibliographic updates to existing references are not new works.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites introduction, related-work, and case-study passages, adds an ablation subsection and acknowledgements, and expands appendix discussion. The overall narrative order is retained, with the method and conclusion largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds six tables covering scalability, ablations, and sensitivity, plus Figure 8 showing two failures. Existing displays are retained with renumbering, relocation, scaling, and limited caption edits. The document also changes from compact pages to letter-size pages with substantially wider margins.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's important lack of direct validation of its three central components through Table 6, while sensitivity tests and explicit failure cases strengthen robustness assessment and clarify applicability limits. These additions substantially improve empirical support without changing the retained benchmark results. Uncertainty reporting remains absent, and Table 1's 5k construction time of 2.9 hours is not reconciled with Figure 3's 4.4 hours, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the stronger diagnostic evidence.
